name: McGill Curl-Up
cues: Hands under the small of your back — keep the natural curve
Lift head, neck and shoulders as one unit, barely off the floor
Breathe out slowly through pursed lips on the lift
mistakes: Curling the neck to the chest
Flattening the low back into the floor
progression: Pyramid sets 6/4/2 with 10-sec holds

name: Bird-Dog
cues: Opposite arm and leg, reach long — not high
Pelvis stays level: imagine a glass of water on your low back
Sweep the floor with your hand to reset each rep
mistakes: Arching the low back to lift the leg higher
progression: Band around the feet for resistance

name: Side Plank (from knees)
cues: Elbow under shoulder, hips stacked
Lift hips until the body is one straight line
Breathe steadily — no breath-holding
mistakes: Holding to shaking failure — stop at form loss
progression: Full side plank from feet (Week 4+)

name: Band Pull-Apart
cues: Arms straight, band to chest, shoulder blades pinch together
Ribs down — no low-back arch
Slow return, 2 seconds
progression: Slow eccentrics, 4-sec return

name: Banded Face Pull
cues: Pull to forehead height, knuckles back, elbows high
Rotate the forearms out at the end — thumbs behind you
Neck stays long, chin slightly tucked
mistakes: Pulling to the chest (that is a row)
progression: Add a 2-sec pause at full rotation

name: Banded Clamshell
cues: Feel it deep in the buttock — that is glute med working
Pelvis does not roll back as the knee opens
Feet stay glued together
mistakes: Rolling the pelvis to fake range
Feeling it at the front of the hip (TFL taking over) — reduce range
progression: Add a side-plank clamshell

name: Banded Glute Bridge
cues: Push knees out into the band the whole rep
Ribs down, squeeze glutes to lift — never arch to finish
Heels drive, toes light
mistakes: Low back arching at the top
Hamstrings cramping (feet too far away — walk them in)
progression: Single-leg glute bridge 3 × 12 / side

name: Banded Side Steps
cues: Soft knees, hips back slightly, toes forward
Stay the same height — no bouncing
Band stays tight every step
progression: Band at ankles, lower stance

name: Pallof Press
cues: Band at chest height, stand side-on, feet shoulder width
Press straight out and resist the rotation — ribs down
Exhale on the press
mistakes: Letting the band twist the torso (that is the load winning)
progression: Half-kneeling Pallof, then split stance

name: Dead Bug (band-assisted)
cues: Low back stays heavy on the floor — that is the whole exercise
Extend one leg slowly while the band holds your arms
Exhale fully before you move
mistakes: Low back arching off the floor as the leg drops
progression: Longer levers, slower tempo

name: 90/90 Hip Switch
cues: Both knees at 90°, rotate like windshield wipers
Go slow into the stiff side — that side is the point
Sit taller as range opens
mistakes: Leaning away to fake the rotation
regression: Hands behind you for support, smaller range
progression: No hands, add a lift-off on the trailing leg

name: Prone Hip IR Rocks
cues: Face down, knee bent 90°, let the foot drop outward slowly
Pelvis stays glued to the floor
Compare sides — note which one barely moves
mistakes: Pelvis lifting off the floor to cheat range
progression: Add a light ankle band resistance

name: Side-Lying Adductor Squeeze
cues: Pillow between the knees, squeeze at 70% effort
Pairs with the 90/90 work — it teaches the inward rotators
Breathe out on the squeeze
progression: Longer holds, 8 sec

name: Half-Kneeling Hip Flexor Stretch
cues: Tuck the tailbone first — squeeze the glute of the back leg
Shift forward only after the tuck; no low-back arch
This is the direct counter to anterior pelvic tilt
mistakes: Arching the low back and calling it a stretch
progression: Add the long band overhead reach

name: Chin Tuck
cues: Glide the chin straight back — make a double chin
Eyes stay level
Tall through the crown of the head
mistakes: Tilting the head down instead of gliding back
progression: Seated with band resistance behind the head

name: Wall Angel
cues: Head, upper back and tailbone on the wall
Slide arms up only as far as contact holds
Ribs down — no arching off the wall
regression: Smaller range, floor angel on your back
progression: Banded wall angel

name: Banded Row
cues: Hinge slightly, spine neutral, pull to the lower ribs
Shoulder blades glide together — chest tall
Ribs down at the finish
mistakes: Rounding the low back to pull harder
progression: One-arm banded row 3 × 12 / side

name: Dowel Hip Hinge
cues: Dowel (or broom handle) touches head, mid-back and tailbone — all three, always
Push the hips back like closing a door with your backside
Stop where contact breaks — that is your current range
mistakes: Rounding to reach lower (the dowel tells you)
Bending the knees into a squat
progression: Banded pull-through 3 × 15

name: Banded Pull-Through
cues: Hinge pattern, glutes snap you upright
Ribs down at the top — squeeze, do not arch
Band anchored low behind you
progression: Heavier band; gym swap: cable pull-through / light kettlebell deadlift 12–16 kg

name: Single-Leg Glute Bridge
cues: Pelvis stays level — no drop on the free side
Extra set on your weaker side, always
Hamstring cramp = feet closer in
progression: Foot elevated single-leg bridge

name: QL Side Reach / Side Bend (gentle)
cues: Small range, smooth breathing — this is mobility, not loading
Gentle side-bend work for the quadratus lumborum
Stop if it refers pain down the leg
mistakes: Loading this move with weight (never in this program)
progression: Standing with wall support

name: Single Knee-to-Chest
cues: ONE knee at a time — never both together
Gentle pull, mild stretch only
Other foot stays planted
mistakes: Pulling both limbs in together at the same time
progression: Add a slow ankle pump during the hold

name: Figure-4 Stretch
cues: Ankle on opposite knee, gentle lean-in
Feel it in the buttock, not the knee
Breathe and let it soften
progression: Pigeon progression on the floor

name: Cat-Camel
cues: Motion, not stretch — move through a comfortable arc
McGill: this reduces stiffness before stability work
Breathe with the movement
progression: Add segmental control — move one vertebra at a time

name: Stability-Ball Wall Squat
cues: Ball or wall supports the back — squat only as deep as symptoms allow
Knees track over toes, heels down
Wall support is a feature while the pattern rebuilds
progression: Banded goblet squat to a box

name: 90/90 March (banded hip control)
cues: Control before load
Band above knees, march tall, pelvis level
Slow — 3 seconds per step
mistakes: Trunk leaning to lift the leg
progression: Standing banded march with a pause

name: 360° Breathing & Brace
cues: Hands on lower ribs — breathe into front, sides and back
Long slow exhale, ribs drop down and in
Finish each exhale with a gentle brace, like bracing for a cough
regression: Supine with knees bent, fewer breaths
progression: Standing brace, then brace while marching in place

name: Doorway Chest Stretch
cues: Forearm on the door frame, elbow at shoulder height
Step through gently until the front of the chest opens
Chin lightly tucked, ribs down — no low-back arch
mistakes: Forcing the shoulder deep into the stretch
Arching the back to feel more stretch
progression: Both arms on a corner, 45 sec holds

name: Scapular Wall Slide
cues: Forearms on the wall, slide up in a narrow V
Keep ribs down and neck long as you slide
Slide only as high as the forearms stay on the wall
progression: Add a mini-band around the wrists

name: Thoracic Open Book
cues: Side-lying, knees stacked and held still — pelvis does not roll
Rotate only through the upper back, follow your hand with your eyes
Exhale as you open; lumbar spine stays quiet
mistakes: Letting the knees and pelvis roll with you (that turns it into lumbar twisting)
regression: Smaller range, pillow under the head
progression: Add a 5-sec hold at end range

name: Supine Deep Neck Flexor Hold
cues: Start with a small chin tuck, then lift the head barely off the floor
Keep the tuck the whole hold — head heavy, effort light
Breathe normally; stop before the front-of-neck muscles take over
mistakes: Lifting high with the big front neck muscles
regression: Chin tuck holds without the lift
progression: Longer holds, up to 20 sec

name: Seated Hip Internal Rotation (banded)
cues: Sit tall on a chair, knee bent 90°, mini-band around the ankles or foot anchored
Rotate the shin outward so the hip turns inward — thigh stays still
Prioritise the stiff (right) side: do it first and add an extra set
mistakes: Thigh swinging or trunk leaning to fake the rotation
regression: No band, smaller range, hands on chair
progression: Slower tempo with a 3-sec end-range hold

name: Standing Hip Internal Rotation Drill
cues: Stand side-on holding a chair, band anchored low pulling the ankle outward
Turn the whole leg inward from the hip — toes, knee and thigh rotate together
Pelvis faces forward the whole rep
mistakes: Rotating the pelvis and trunk instead of the hip
regression: No band, hand on chair, smaller range
progression: No chair support, slower tempo

name: 90/90 Internal Rotation Lift-Off
cues: From the 90/90 position, in the trailing-leg (internal rotation) side
Lift the ankle off the floor using only the hip — no trunk lean
Tiny range is fine; this is end-range strength, not mobility
mistakes: Leaning the trunk away to lift the foot
Cramps or sharp hip pinch — stop and reduce range
progression: Add a light ankle weight or band resistance

name: Supine Pelvic Tilt Drill
cues: On your back, knees bent — gently roll the pelvis so the waistband tips up
Use deep abdominals and glutes, small pain-free range only
This teaches the posterior tilt the hip-flexor stretch needs
mistakes: Big, forceful tilting into end range
regression: Smaller range, hands under pelvis for feedback
progression: Progress to dead bug toe taps keeping the tilt

name: Standing Rectus Femoris Stretch
cues: Hold a chair, bend one knee and hold the ankle (or a towel loop) behind you
Tuck the tailbone and squeeze that glute first, then ease the knee back
Thighs stay side by side — no low-back arch
mistakes: Arching the back to pull the foot higher
Pulling the ankle hard into the buttock
progression: Half-kneeling version with a pad under the knee

name: Side-Lying Hip Abduction
cues: Side-lying, top leg straight and slightly behind the body line
Lift from the deep buttock, toes pointing slightly down
Keep the pelvis stacked — no rolling back
mistakes: Rolling the pelvis back and using the front of the hip
Lifting the leg high with a trunk lean
progression: Add a mini-band above the knees

name: Banded Standing Glute Kickback
cues: Mini-band above the ankles, hold a chair, hinge very slightly
Drive the heel back a short way by squeezing the glute
Pelvis stays square — the low back does not arch to finish
mistakes: Kicking high and arching the low back
progression: Slower tempo with a 2-sec squeeze at the back

name: Prone Hip Extension (glute firing)
cues: Face down, forehead on hands, gentle abdominal brace first
Lift one straight leg a few inches by squeezing the glute first
Hamstring may help — low back should stay quiet
mistakes: Low back firing first or arching to lift
progression: Add a mini-band above the knees

name: Suitcase Carry
cues: One light dumbbell at your side, stand tall as if balancing a book on your head
Walk slowly — do not lean away from the weight
Ribs down, opposite side (QL and obliques) does the holding
mistakes: Leaning away from or into the weight
Shrugging the shoulder to the ear
regression: Lighter dumbbell, stand in place marching
progression: Heavier dumbbell, longer walks up to 60 sec / side

name: Seated QL Stretch
cues: Sit tall on a chair, one hand overhead reaching gently to the opposite side
Keep both sit-bones down and breathe into the stretched side
Gentle stretch only — this is a cool-down, not a loaded side bend
regression: Smaller reach, hand on thigh for support
progression: Standing version with wall support

name: Prone Back Extension Hold (unloaded)
cues: Face down, arms at your sides, lift the chest a small way using the back muscles
Range stays small and pain-free — this is endurance, not height
Glutes lightly on, neck in line with the spine
mistakes: Leg pain or pain that travels down the leg — stop
regression: Chest supported on a pillow, smaller lift
progression: Longer holds, up to 20 sec, or add slow arm reaches

name: Sphinx (Prone on Elbows)
cues: Face down on forearms, elbows under shoulders, hips and legs relaxed
Only use if extension eases your symptoms — stop if leg pain increases
Breathe slowly and let the back settle
mistakes: Pushing into pain or forcing height
Using it on an extension-intolerant day
regression: Prone lying flat on a pillow instead
progression: Progress to prone press-up only if this stays symptom-free

name: Prone Press-Up
cues: Face down, hands under shoulders, press the chest up while the pelvis stays on the floor
Only use if extension clearly eases your symptoms — never push through leg pain
Move slowly, partial range is fine
mistakes: Continuing if pain moves further down the leg
progression: Full press-ups with 2-sec holds at the top

name: Sciatic Nerve Glide
cues: Sit tall or lie on your back with a towel behind the thigh, knee bent
Gently straighten the knee a little while pointing the toes away, then bend it as you pull the toes toward you — a slow see-saw
This is a glide, not a stretch: stay well short of any sharp or electric pull
mistakes: Holding a hard hamstring stretch position
progression: Slightly larger range, still pain-free

name: 90/90 Hamstring Lower (active control)
cues: On your back, hip and knee at 90°, hands behind the thigh
Slowly straighten the knee as far as control allows, then lower the whole leg a few inches
Keep the low back heavy on the floor — control, not stretch-chasing
mistakes: Yanking the leg straight with a towel
Low back arching off the floor
progression: Slower 5-sec lowers

name: Low Step-Up
cues: Use a low step or sturdy chair seat edge height you can control
Whole foot on the step, drive up through the heel using the glute
Pelvis level, knee tracks over the toes
mistakes: Pushing off hard with the back foot
regression: Lower step, hand on wall or chair for balance
progression: Higher step, slower tempo, light dumbbell in the opposite hand

name: Constructive Rest Breathing
cues: Lie on your back, calves resting on a chair seat, hips and knees at about 90°
Let the low back settle heavy into the floor
Slow nasal breathing — longer exhales than inhales
mistakes: Using it to avoid all movement on normal days (it is for cool-down and flares)
progression: Add gentle pelvic tilts in this position
